title: Why Your Ears Pop On A Plane
sources: Mayo Clinic: Airplane ear (ear barotrauma): cabin pressure changes on climb/descent, eustachian tube, swallowing, yawning, chewing gum
Merck / MSD Manual: Barotrauma of the ear (eustachian tube equalizes middle-ear pressure)
Altru Health / Frommer's: airplane ear, open the tube by yawning, swallowing, chewing gum

lines.text: Why do your ears pop on a plane?
Behind each eardrum, there's a tiny pocket of air,
connected to your throat by a thin tube.
When the plane climbs, the air in the cabin gets thinner,
so the air trapped in your ear pushes your eardrum outward!
Then you swallow or yawn, and the tube opens for a split second,
the pressure evens out, and... pop!
That's why chewing gum helps on a flight:
every swallow opens the tube again.
Try it right now: swallow, and listen!
